missesUnderReview: steady-state-fps-p50: 28.5 fps against the >= 60 fps target
steady-state-fps-p95: 8.6 fps against the >= 55 fps target
evidence: The 60 fps target was written for a mid-tier laptop with a visible window; this measurement runs headless on Intel UHD Graphics (integrated), 1280x800, devicePixelRatio 1.

The measurement is not stable enough to gate: three back-to-back 2s windows in one run gave p50 31.4 / 14.0 / 28.5 fps (61.1% spread), and separate runs on the same build and hardware ranged from 7.7 to 37.9 fps p50. CPU load measured 19% during the slow readings, so the variance is not CPU saturation.
The same scene at 640x400 measures p50 59.9 fps and p95 58.8 fps, so the cost scales with pixel count: the M0 viewer is fill-rate bound, not scene-graph bound (13 draw calls, 3984 triangles).
Removing the frame-rate limit makes rAF deltas meaningless (p50 909 fps, p95 16.6 fps bimodal), so the vsync-paced measurement is the only honest one.
First 3D paint is 821 ms against a 3000 ms budget, and draw calls are 13 against 150, so neither load time nor scene complexity is the constraint.
proposedOptions: Keep 60 fps as the target and treat this as an open M1 performance item: drop clearcoat from the large translucent shell (MeshPhysicalMaterial -> MeshStandardMaterial), prefer FrontSide where DoubleSide is not required, and apply the D12 DPR cap and quality tier (task 4.8).
Re-ratify the target per hardware tier: >= 40 fps p50 on integrated GPUs while idle, with 60 fps retained for discrete-GPU machines.
Defer the decision to M2, re-measure on a quiet machine with a process animating, and require at least three runs before treating any fps number as a baseline.
ratification.note: Recorded, not accepted. No target was lowered and no number here was chosen to look better: the committed value is the median of a run whose own windows disagreed by 61%, which is the honest representation of what this machine produced. The maintainer decides which option applies.

notes: Draw calls, payload sizes and file sizes hard-fail CI: they are deterministic.
Frame timing is advisory by design — CI runners share GPUs and jitter — so p50/p95 are recorded here and reviewed locally.
Draw calls and triangles are now measured on the composed cell fixture, which is what the per-cell budget was always about; the organelle block remains the single-organelle reading.

The quality tier is read from the running app rather than inferred. Under a fixture it is pinned to high so a screenshot cannot depend on the host core count; the adaptive path is unit-tested and only runs in the real app.
